topic: Eneva acquisition of Ceiba/Jandaia and 2030 Pecém terminal timeline
wiki_text: In April 2025 Eneva signed a share purchase agreement to acquire Ceiba Energy's Jandaia power station together with the associated Pecém LNG terminal project; Brazil's antitrust authority Cade approved the deal in late May 2025 and the acquisition was concluded in early September 2025. In the March 2026 capacity-reserve (reserva de capacidade) auction, Eneva and Diamante won a contract for a new gas-fired thermal plant at the Pecém Complex (Jandaia), with reported investment of R$6.5 billion plus a R$430 million dedicated natural-gas pier ('Píer Zero'). Gas is to be supplied by an FSRU permanently moored at the Port of Pecém, with terminal operations targeted for 2030 and construction beginning in the first half of 2026. The specific FSRU vessel has not been publicly confirmed.

topic: 2025 operations halt, Energos Winter relocation, and ANP restart options
wiki_text: In July 2025 New Fortress Energy halted operations at Terminal Gás Sul, citing uncertainty over Brazil's next backup-capacity tender, and relocated the Energos Winter FSRU to Egypt under a five-year charter with EGAS (the vessel took its first cargo at the Damietta terminal around October 2025). NFE subsequently submitted two alternative restart timelines to Brazil's ANP, targeting re-berthing of an FSRU at the Santa Catarina terminal in either July 2026 or July 2027, tying reactivation to the outcome of the March 2026 capacity-reserve auction.

topic: Associated CELBA 2 power plant first fire (Oct 2025)
wiki_text: New Fortress Energy achieved first fire at the 624 MW CELBA 2 power plant in Barcarena (Pará) on October 6, 2025, beginning hot commissioning, with commercial operation expected later in 2025. The plant is fed by regasified LNG from NFE's Barcarena terminal (Energos Celsius FSRU), part of a 2.2 GW Barcarena power complex (CELBA 2 plus the PortoCem plant). Per EIA, the Barcarena terminal's CELBA 2 phase began operating around October 2025 at ~0.75 Bcf/d. (Power-plant detail; recorded here for terminal context, not a terminal capacity change.)

As of late 2025 the Suape FSRU (Aruanã Energia / OnCorp) in Pernambuco remained under construction, with completion expected in early 2026 and the FSRU expected operational by the end of 2026 (~0.7 Bcf/d). In May 2025 OnCorp announced it had signed an agreement for the FSRU to be moored at Suape, with greater storage capacity than originally planned, and that Shell would supply the LNG processed at the terminal.
